A.reason: It is the only collection here lacking the perfect fifth above the tonic and carrying a tritone over it, so the tonic is never structurally supported and no degree offers a negotiated resolution.

B.reason: Maximally consonant support for the tonic (major third, perfect fourth and fifth) with its single tritone displaced away from the tonic and a semitone leading upward into it, so every degree is defined by a fixed position relative to a centre that holds.

C.reason: Bright raised fourth gives the highest raised-minus-lowered count, yet that same degree forms a tritone against the tonic that never settles, so the collection sounds like an inflated brightness measured against a centre it keeps overshooting.

D.reason: Its step pattern is a palindrome, so the collection maps onto itself under inversion and is the only one whose structure is literally cyclic rather than directed, which is the nearest structural analogue to fixed periodicity.

A.reason: No further degradation is available within these seven: absence of the perfect fifth plus a tritone over the tonic is already the limiting case, so extremity adds intensity but no change of collection.

B.reason: The perfect fifth is retained, so the order still holds, but the flattened second clamps the tonic from a semitone above, turning positional definition into pressure exerted at the smallest possible interval.

C.reason: At the extreme the reflecting term fails: removing the perfect fifth leaves the tonic with no consonant support to be measured against, so the comparison that organised the state loses its fixed point.

D.reason: The ground for the choice was the palindromic step structure, which is a property of the collection and is unaffected by how extreme or painful the state is said to be.

unmatchable_reason: A, B and C each specify a relation to a centre or limit that interval content can model (presence or absence of the perfect fifth, placement of the tritone, semitone approach to the tonic), whereas D specifies only periodicity of attention, a temporal property with no affective valence and no pitch correlate; my M2/S3 choices rest on a formal analogy between palindromic step patterns and cyclicity, which is decoration, not a principled mapping.

A.reason: No perfect fifth, a tritone over the tonic, and adjacent semitones clustered at the bottom of the collection, so the tonic is both unsupported and crowded, with nothing that resolves.

B.reason: Perfect fifth present and no tritone at all, with matched semitones sitting directly above the tonic and above the fifth, giving a rigid frame of fixed positions around two stable poles.

C.reason: Highest raised-minus-lowered count of the set, but the raised fourth puts a tritone over the tonic, so the brightness is inflated against a centre it never plainly confirms.

D.reason: Its step pattern 1-3-1-2-1-3-1 is a palindrome, making it the one rotation here that maps onto itself, the only structural stand-in for a fixed cycle.

recognised_family: The diatonic (church) modes, i.e. the seven rotations of the major scale.
source_of_part3: The assignments were made on interval content, chiefly presence or absence of the perfect fifth, the placement of the tritone relative to the tonic, and semitone approach to the tonic; the conventional mode names were known and their received affective glosses agree in places, but that agreement is largely because both track the same raised-minus-lowered degree count, and where the received glosses go beyond that (for instance Lydian as simply euphoric) I did not follow them.
